townName: Diocletian's Palace and the Old Town
seoTitle: Split cruise port guide: walk to Diocletian's Palace
seoDescription: Split's cruise berths are 5–20 min on foot from Diocletian's Palace. Palace streets free, cellars €10 (2026). Trogir bus €2.50 by app. Board 60 min early.
quickAnswer: Most ships dock in Split's city port, either on the inner quays near the Riva (5–10 minutes' walk to Diocletian's Palace) or on the outer berths of the St Duje breakwater (15–20 minutes); some ships anchor and tender. You need no transport for the Old Town. Start walking back from the Riva 90 minutes before all-aboard if you are on the breakwater, 75 minutes if you are on the inner quays.
intro: Split is a working city built into a Roman emperor's retirement palace, and the cruise berths sit right beside it. The palace streets, Peristyle and gates are free and open all day, so a cruise day here costs very little unless you add the cellars, cathedral and bell tower. The question is less how to get to town than what to add: Marjan Hill and Bačvice beach are walkable, Trogir and Klis need a bus or taxi, and Krka needs a very long call. Ferries, catamarans and coaches share the same harbour, so the waterfront road is busy from early morning.
tenderNotes: Split is mainly a docking port, but anchorage and tendering are permitted and some ships tender when berths are full. Tender landings are closer to the Old Town than the outer breakwater berths; your ship will confirm the landing point.

terminals.name: Inner city-port quays (Riva end of the harbour)
terminals.notes: Shared with ferries. 5–10 minutes' flat walk to the palace's Bronze Gate on the Riva.

terminals.name: Outer berths, St Duje breakwater (Gat sv. Duje)
terminals.notes: Two berths built for large ships (up to about 320 m and 265–270 m). 15–20 minutes' walk along the harbour road; some lines run a shuttle to the Riva.

walkability.detail: Flat and paved all the way round the harbour to the Riva. There is little shade on the breakwater and the harbour road is busy with ferry traffic and coaches. Allow 20 minutes from the far end of the breakwater.

transportSections.detail: Follow the harbour edge west to the Riva promenade; the Bronze Gate into the palace cellars is halfway along it.
Some ships on the breakwater run a shuttle to the Riva. Ask at the gangway rather than assuming.

transportSections.cost: €2.50 by app, ticket machine or office; €5 from the driver (2026)
transportSections.detail: Trogir is in Promet's fourth price class. Buy through the Promet app or a ticket office to pay half the driver price.

transportSections.cost: €1.50 by app or ticket office; €3 from the driver (2026)
transportSections.detail: Useful for Marjan or Žnjan if you do not want to walk. Fares rose 50% on 1 June 2026.
A taxi rank serves the port. Uber operates in Split. A pre-booked car to Trogir takes about 35–40 minutes each way.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard: leave the Riva by 16:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard if you are on the breakwater, by 16:15 from the inner quays.
returnTiming.detail: The walk back to the outer berths takes 15–20 minutes, plus security at the gangway. Ferry departures in the late afternoon can block the harbour road with queuing cars and foot passengers. If you go to Trogir, aim to be back in Split by 15:30, as coastal traffic towards Split builds in the afternoon.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: From Trogir or Klis, take a taxi or Uber straight to your berth rather than waiting for a bus. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme.

excursionAdvice: You do not need a ship tour for Split itself: the palace is beside the ship and the streets are free. A ship excursion is worth paying for to Krka National Park (about 1.5 hours each way, only realistic on a 9–10 hour call), to the islands by boat, or if you want Trogir and Klis in one day without managing buses. For Trogir alone, the bus or a pre-booked driver is cheaper and works on a normal call.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking on the St Duje breakwater at 08:00, a 17:30 all-aboard and a summer weekday.

steps.what: Walk round the harbour to the Riva (15–20 minutes).
Enter the palace through the Bronze Gate and walk the free central cellar corridor up to the Peristyle.
Climb the cathedral bell tower before the tour groups arrive, then visit the Cathedral of St Domnius and Jupiter's Temple.
Walk out through the Golden Gate to the Grgur Ninski statue, then through the Iron Gate to People's Square.
Lunch in Varoš, for example Konoba Fetivi (closed Sundays).
Walk up Marjan Hill to the first viewpoint above Varoš, or swim at Bačvice.
Back on board, one hour before all-aboard.

sights.name: Diocletian's Palace and the Peristyle
sights.why: A Roman emperor's palace from around AD 300 that is still lived in, with the Peristyle as its central square.
sights.tip: The streets and all four gates are open 24 hours. Come before 09:30 or after 16:00 for space.

sights.name: Palace cellars (substructures)
sights.why: The vaulted halls under the palace, which preserve its original floor plan.
sights.cost: €10 for the east and west halls; central corridor free (2026)
sights.tip: Cool in summer, so save it for late morning.

sights.name: Cathedral of St Domnius and bell tower
sights.why: Diocletian's mausoleum turned cathedral, with a 57 m Romanesque bell tower over the Peristyle.
sights.cost: Separate and combined tickets; combinations reported at about €7–15 (2026)
sights.tip: Shoulders and knees covered. The tower stairs are steep and narrow near the top.

sights.name: Jupiter's Temple
sights.why: Small Roman temple later used as a baptistery, with a carved coffered ceiling.
sights.cost: €4, or part of some cathedral combinations (2026)
sights.tip: Check whether your cathedral ticket already covers it.

sights.name: Riva promenade
sights.why: The palm-lined waterfront along the palace's south wall.
sights.tip: Cafés here are pricier than in Varoš or around People's Square.

sights.name: Marjan Hill
sights.why: Wooded park on the peninsula west of the centre, with steps up to viewpoints over the city and islands.
sights.tip: The first viewpoint is about 15–20 minutes' climb up steps from Varoš. Take water.

sights.name: Trogir
sights.why: Small walled UNESCO town on an islet 30 km west.
sights.tip: Go in the morning; afternoon traffic back towards Split is slower.

sights.name: Klis Fortress
sights.why: Hilltop fortress above Split with wide views; a Game of Thrones location.
sights.tip: Buses are infrequent; a taxi or Uber is safer on a cruise day.

beaches.name: Bačvice
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk east from the port and ferry terminal
beaches.note: Shallow, sandy-pebble city beach. Busy and lively in summer; home of the local ball game picigin.

beaches.name: Kasjuni
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi or bus towards the south side of Marjan
beaches.note: Pebble cove below Marjan, quieter than Bačvice.

food.where: Villa Spiza (small, cash only, closed Sundays)
Pazar market by the Silver Gate
Konobas around Varoš and outside the palace walls

commonMistakes.fix: The palace streets, gates and Peristyle are free. Only the cellars, cathedral, bell tower and temple charge.

commonMistakes.mistake: Climbing the bell tower at midday.
commonMistakes.fix: Go first thing; the stairs are narrow and queues build when groups arrive.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying bus tickets from the driver.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the Promet app or a ticket office: driver tickets cost double since June 2026.
Krka needs about 9–10 hours in port. Do Trogir or Klis instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Underestimating the walk back to the breakwater.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow 20 minutes plus gangway security. Leave the Riva 90 minutes before all-aboard.

safety: Split is safe for visitors. Watch for pickpockets in the crowded palace lanes, on the Riva and around the bus and ferry terminals. Polished limestone in the palace is slippery when wet. The harbour road carries ferry traffic and coaches, so use crossings. In summer, carry water and shade up between 12:00 and 15:00.
scams: Paid photos with costumed 'Roman soldiers' at the Peristyle: they expect money for a photo, so agree before you pose or decline.
Fish priced per kilo: ask for the weight and total price before the fish is cooked.
Paying double on the bus: drivers charge twice the app or ticket-office fare; this is legal but avoidable.
accessibility: The route from the berths to the Riva is flat and paved. The Riva is level and smooth. Inside the palace, the Peristyle and main lanes are reachable step-free from the Riva side through the cellar corridor, though surfaces are uneven, and some gates have steps. The bell tower and Marjan viewpoints are stairs only. On tender days, ask the ship about wheelchair transfers.
rainyDay: Spend the time in the palace cellars, the cathedral and Jupiter's Temple, then the covered fish market and the cafés around People's Square. The palace's limestone is very slippery in rain, so wear shoes with grip.
crowdTips: Split receives over 260 cruise calls a year and also handles heavy ferry traffic to the islands, so the waterfront is busy whatever the cruise schedule. Tour groups pack the Peristyle and the cellar corridor from about 09:30 to 12:30. Do the bell tower first, then move outward to Varoš, Marjan or Bačvice while groups are in the palace. Late afternoon on the Riva is calmer than midday.

faqs.q: Is Split cruise port walkable to the Old Town?
faqs.a: Yes. Inner quays are 5–10 minutes from the Riva; the outer breakwater berths are 15–20 minutes, all flat.
Mostly no. Ships usually dock in the city port; tendering is allowed and some ships use it when berths are taken.
The streets, gates and Peristyle are free. The cellars cost €10 and the cathedral, bell tower and temple have separate or combined tickets (2026).

faqs.q: How do I get from Split cruise port to Trogir?
faqs.a: Take a Promet bus (€2.50 by app, €5 from the driver in 2026) or a taxi or Uber, about 35–40 minutes by car.

faqs.q: What can I do in Split in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The palace, cathedral and cellars in the morning, lunch in Varoš, then Marjan Hill or Bačvice beach.

faqs.q: Are there beaches near Split cruise port?
faqs.a: Bačvice is 5–10 minutes' walk east of the port. Kasjuni, below Marjan, is quieter but needs a taxi or bus.

faqs.q: Is Split safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Watch for pickpockets in the palace and on the Riva.

faqs.q: Can I visit Krka from Split on a cruise?
faqs.a: Only on a long call of about 9–10 hours. Otherwise choose Trogir or Klis.
